title: 3.1 Notation and Background
use_cases: Configure when training a language model to maximize a reward function while maintaining proximity to a reference model
Implement when data-limited expert demonstrations are available instead of large-scale human comparison datasets
Use when designing a loss function that incorporates KL-constraint modulation via alpha
Apply when aiming to overcome priors induced by standard RLHF training through synthetic comparison generation

While this objective is ubiquitous in prior work (Ouyang et al., 2022; Rafailov et al., 2023), it is typically applied in the context of population-based reward functions learned from large comparison datasets collected via a multitude of annotators. In contrast, we consider r⁢(x,y)𝑟𝑥𝑦r(x,y)italic_r ( italic_x , italic_y ) to be the objective of a single individual. In this regime, collecting thousands of comparisons from one user is infeasible. Instead, we assume access to a small dataset of expert demonstrations, denoted 𝒟Esubscript𝒟𝐸\mathcal{D}_{E}caligraphic_D start_POSTSUBSCRIPT italic_E end_POSTSUBSCRIPT. While demonstrations are typically used for SFT, such approaches typically struggle in data-limited settings. On the other hand, it can be difficult to prompt a model to “overcome” the priors induced by its RLHF training. DITTO, as described in the next section, addresses these problems by directly generating comparison data using LM outputs and expert demonstrations.
